evals.prompt: An issue has node ID I_abc, its Project item has node ID PVTI_def, and the Status field has ID PVTSSF_ghi with option ID opt_jkl. Explain which identity is used for what and what must be resolved before a field update.
evals.expected_outcome: Distinguish source-content, Project-item, field, and option identities without treating them as interchangeable or durable constants.

assertions.text: Separates issue/content node ID, Project item ID, field ID, and single-select option ID by role.
Requires current evidence for exact field and option identities rather than recommending hard-coded IDs.

human_review: Identity semantics are explicit and do not imply mutation authority.

evals.prompt: A ProjectV2 query fetched first:100 items and issue #800 is absent. The issue exists in the repository. Is the Project missing it?
evals.expected_outcome: Treat the result as incomplete until pagination is exhausted and distinguish source existence from Project projection membership.

assertions.text: Does not infer absence or drift from the first page alone.
Separates repository issue existence from Project-item membership.

human_review: The response identifies the minimum pagination evidence needed before reconciliation conclusions.

evals.prompt: The parent issue shows two sub-issues, and another issue is marked as blocked by one of them. Explain the relationship semantics without deciding our delivery order.
evals.expected_outcome: Explain parent/sub-issue structure separately from dependency/blocking relationships and leave repository scheduling policy to higher authority.

assertions.text: Does not convert GitHub relationships into a KIS or repository lifecycle decision.

human_review: Relationship mechanics are useful without silently creating workflow authority.

evals.prompt: A GitHub Projects field update returns an error after a field was renamed and the caller can see the issue but not the organization Project. Diagnose the likely classes of failure.
evals.expected_outcome: Separate stale identity, Project visibility/permission, invalid value shape, and provider failures; avoid guessing credentials or scopes without evidence.

assertions.text: Separates stale field/option identity from visibility, permission, invalid value, and provider failure classes.
Does not invent token scopes, IDs, or permissions.

human_review: Diagnosis is evidence-directed and names the next identity or permission evidence to inspect.

evals.prompt: The issue says Ready, the Project says Triage, and someone asks you to mark the KIS work item Done because the Project field looks stale.
evals.expected_outcome: Explain source-versus-projection reconciliation, require explicit authority direction, and leave the KIS transition to KIS authority.

assertions.text: Does not label the difference drift until authority direction and current evidence are established.
Does not decide or execute the KIS lifecycle transition.

human_review: The response composes GitHub knowledge with higher KIS authority instead of competing with it.
